newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turkish Cypriots in peace demonstration.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Cypriots in peace demonstration.

text.p: Thousands of Turkish Cypriots gathered in the north of the island's divided capital to express support for talks being held in the United States between the rival Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities.
Witnesses said crowds listened to concerts and watched fireworks displays on Wednesday night at a small stadium in the Turkish Cypriot sector of Nicosia.
Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides, leader of the Greek Cypriots, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash began five days of U.N.-sponsored talks in upstate New York on Wednesday.
Neither side expects a breakthrough in the 23-year-old division of the Mediterranean island.

"To go down in history as the two leaders who brought peace to Cyprus is a much more human, just and correct approach than to be recalled as the winner of the destroyed, burned down Cyprus," said a statement read out at the Nicosia gathering.
Peace activists said they had send copies of the statement to Denktash, Clerides, U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan and other mediators.
Cyprus has been split since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a short-lived Greek Cypriot coup backed by Athens.
